issue: #577 — Flat reversion P5, family rebind lane C, transition-trace (Q21), on spec #565
spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §4, §7.1, §7.3, §8.8, §10 — fields 0 and 2 of a disputed L2 transaction read through the §8.8 door under authenticate-once, and the forced-order path re-derived from the transaction id alone
note: Lane C's rolling re-measurement, attached as this lane's exit criterion per #565's measurement-slotting rule (AC3). Q21 has two rebound call sites and they move in opposite directions, so both are pinned rather than only the one that improved. `validate_l2_transaction_transition` replaces a decode of each preimage followed by a `field_commitment_from_items` re-hash of the reproduced item list with two door openings via the #575 `FieldOpeningV1` bridge; `tx_order_compact_body` replaces the retired proof-source triple and its commitment check with `verify_native_tx_compact_cbor_v1` against the tx id. Measured against HEAD b824ad6e: the forced-order row falls 3,194,009 → 3,034,025 mem (-5.0%), and the L2 row rises 2,533,821 → 2,760,481 mem (+8.9%). The rise is bought deliberately and its cause is exact: this is the wave's first script to open TWO fields, and `opened_field_walk` re-derives the transaction id from the compact bytes on each opening, so the id is derived three times where one would do (~211k mem apiece). Reaching `authenticated_field_view` directly with a single pre-verified structure measures ~2.34M — below HEAD — but puts this file outside `carriage_reaches_the_anchor` and its §2.5 body/witness pairing, which is the guard #575 closed a reproduced forgery with. A multi-field opening that pays the anchor check once belongs in `field_opening_v1` itself and is deferred to #584 rather than taken unilaterally from a lane running beside three others; #584 carries this row as the number the fix has to beat. NO new unbounded walk is introduced: the door's O(N) walk is over the same preimage the retired decode already walked, and the retired path additionally re-encoded every item, so there is no `basisFit:"exceeds"` row and no infeasibility string. What these rows do NOT claim is a cardinality envelope: each is one vector at one spend input and one output, and the family's cost at high cardinality is dominated by the per-item MPF delete/insert in `apply_l2_spends`/`apply_l2_outputs`, which this lane does not touch and does not measure. Rows are whole-test readings taken through `run-focused-check.mjs`, so they include fixture construction as well as validator execution — the same convention `native-tx-q31-exec-ledger-v1.json` uses, and the reason a row moves when a fixture is simplified. Regenerate with `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN=<fork> node scripts/verify-q21-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move any reported number in the same commit. Provisional: formal closure is Phase 7's, against the Phase-6 blueprint. `--update` rewrites the raw mem/cpu rows; it does NOT rewrite `basisFit`, and it is not a bypass — structural failures (a row or selector that did not run, or a fresh reading that contradicts a `within` judgement by exceeding the basis) fail in update mode too and the ledger is not rewritten.

basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3 — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. Provenance, exactly as §3.3 states it: the captured in-repo artifact is the mainnet parameter snapshot in docs/midgard/decisions/0001-cardano-l1-transaction-capability-floor.md, Conway epoch 645, observed 2026-07-24. The report that the cap is unchanged at epoch 648 is corroboration only — no protocol-params artifact in this repository pins epoch 648.

modules.neutralisationNote: Every selector is mutation-verified rather than assumed, and each is listed against the mutation that turns it red. The two rebound call sites need different vectors, so both sets are here. (1) and (2), `rejects_l2_transaction_with_a_substituted_spend_inputs_preimage` and `rejects_l2_transaction_with_a_substituted_outputs_preimage`: neutralising `whole_view`'s `expect field_commitment(preimage) == expected_hash` in `lib/midgard/native-tx-field-access-v1.ak` turns exactly these two red and nothing else in the module — they hold the §7.1 authenticate-once check for the L2 row's two door openings. (3) `rejects_l2_transaction_with_wrong_authenticated_transaction_id`: neutralising the anchor check `expect native_tx_id_for_version(version, body_cbor) == native_tx_id` in `lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/native-tx/compact.ak` turns exactly this one red. That check is what BOTH rebound call sites rest on — the L2 row's `verify_native_tx_compact_cbor_v1` and the forced-order row's `tx_order_compact_body` — and no door selector sees it, because the door is reached only once the anchor has been accepted. (4) `accepts_omitted_forced_order_at_authenticated_end_time_boundary`: the forced-order row asserts `!forced_event_is_due(...)`, so a due-check degenerating to always-False would satisfy that row for free; forcing `forced_event_is_due` to False turns exactly this selector red and leaves every other test in the module green, selector (5) included. It is a positive test used as a neutralisation selector for precisely that reason — the vacuity direction of a negated guard is only provable by a test that needs the guard to say yes. (5) `rejects_omitted_forced_order_published_after_challenged_block`: forcing `forced_event_is_due` to True turns this, `rejects_omitted_forced_order_at_excluded_start_time_boundary` and the forced-order row itself red. It brackets the authenticated window from the other side, at the same `end_time + 1` inclusion time the row is measured at. Two vectors are deliberately NOT listed, both because they survive the door mutation: `rejects_l2_transaction_with_uncommitted_spend_preimage`, because `apply_l2_spends` rejects its mismatched delete witness before the door is ever the reason, and `rejects_l2_transaction_with_a_miscounted_committed_spend_inputs_preimage`, which two independent door guards refuse, so it isolates neither.
